## Area of the trapezoids

Let's find the area of the first trapezoid:

$\begin{align}
\text{Area}_1 &= (1-(-1)) \cdot \dfrac{g(-1)+g(1)}{2} \\\\
&= 2\cdot \dfrac{16}{2} \\ \\
&=16
\end{align}$

##The plan

We can find the area of each trapezoid by multiplying its width by the average of the values of $g(x)$ at the left and right endpoints.

![A trapezoid whose bases are vertical has width b minus a. The left, shorter base has height g of a. The right, taller base has height g of b.](web+graphie:${☣ LOCALPATH}/images/30fd077dee33799f28834d5d2c9bacf04cc68015) 

$\text{area of trapezoid}=(b-a)\left( \dfrac{g(a)+g(b)}{2} \right)$

Then we *sum* all of the areas.

We can repeat the process for the remaining trapezoids.

$\begin{align}
\text{Area}_2 &= (3-1) \cdot \dfrac{g(1)+g(3)}{2} \\\\
&= 2\cdot \dfrac{7}{2} \\ \\
&=7
\end{align}$

$\begin{align}
\text{Area}_3 &= (5-3) \cdot \dfrac{g(3)+g(5)}{2} \\\\
&= 2\cdot \dfrac{9}{2} \\ \\
&=9
\end{align}$
